why: One learned, ageless cell a head (one1-st-mps) brought 140% of the copying gain of 128 knowledge cells on the second showing of random letters (knowledge_and_plasticity.json): the gain looks like the option to answer that nothing here fits, as attention sinks do in Transformers. But how well a test bed copies varies by about a bit a byte from seed to seed (test_bed_with_delays.json), so one seed cannot carry the claim.

arms.sink-sS: the delayed test bed with one knowledge cell a head (--read-knowledge 1 --granule-cells 1021), seeds 20001 to 20004
arms.bed-sS: the delayed test bed, seeds 20002 to 20004; seed 20001 is combo-bed of knowledge_and_plasticity.json

training: On streams (--stream 10 --stream-groups 3), 6,000 updates, on the server's CPU, exactly as combo-bed (code v17d), every pair sharing its seed and data order
measure: The copy probe (experiments/copy_probe.py: random letters and random words shown twice) for every arm, and the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams (lead 8,192, pieces of 512) with the bits of every piece kept.
pass_mark: The sink is the copying gain if sink-sS copies random letters better than bed-sS on their second showing at all four seeds, by at least 0.3 bits a byte on average. Its effect on the long streams is reported beside it, paired by seed.
seen_before_recording: One seed on the laptop's GPU (one1-st-mps against g6d-st-mps and know128-st-mps); no run of these arms exists.
